paragraphs.tag: MAP: gm-1 | cold open, ending first: wide tilted terrain Vicksburg - Big Black - Jackson; watch box 17 MAY 1863 SUNDAY; distance card; the bridge on fire; Grant medallion; title card over the map
paragraphs.text: On the seventeenth of May 1863, east of Vicksburg, a Confederate army burned the bridge behind it. The fire was meant to stop Ulysses Grant. It stopped him for one day. This is the story of the Big Black River, and the bridge that burned to save Vicksburg.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: gm-2 | cloud dive into the close 3D battlefield; Pemberton medallion; red bridgehead on the east bank, blue divisions arriving from the east; watch box switches to the clock; bottom timeline appears
paragraphs.text: The day before, at Champion Hill, Pemberton had lost a whole division. Now his men held the crossing of the Big Black, with the river at their back.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: gm-3 | the assault: solid blue arrows, clock to ~9:00, event tag BIG BLACK BRIDGE BURNED, counter PRISONERS to 1,751, UNION LOSS 279, ledger entry 1
paragraphs.text: By mid-morning, it was over. A little after nine, Grant tells us in his Memoirs, the line was taken. Behind it, the bridge burned. Eighteen guns. 1,751 prisoners, by his count. Some six for every Union soldier hit.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: gm-4 | flashback banner A MONTH EARLIER; watch box in date mode 16 APRIL 1863 THURSDAY 10 P.M.; oval painting inset (transports running the batteries, LoC); quote card with source line
paragraphs.text: Grant had seen fire on the river before. One April night, his boats ran past the guns of Vicksburg. A steamer burned to the water's edge, and drifted on downstream. Grant watched from the deck.

paragraphs.tag: MAP: gm-5 | back on the close map: three new bridges, blue boxes crossing west; ledger entries 2-4 + stamp ONE DAY
paragraphs.text: By the next day, three new bridges crossed the river. The fire had stopped him for one day.
